intro: Candidates for this exam should have expertise in automating software development workflows with GitHub Actions. This includes creating and maintaining workflows and actions, managing GitHub Actions at scale, and ensuring secure and efficient automation for organizations and enterprises. Candidates should also be familiar with CI/CD, GitHub repositories, GitHub Packages, and integrating third-party services.

foundations.title: Introduction to Git
foundations.why: Teaches version control and basic Git commands, the repository concepts that push and pull request events are built on.

foundations.title: Introduction to DevOps
foundations.why: Gives the DevOps and source control background (what source control is, how Git works locally) that automated workflows assume, at an introductory level.

foundations.title: Introduction to GitHub
foundations.why: Introduces GitHub and the GitHub flow of repositories and collaboration, the platform concepts the workflow events attach to.

foundations.title: Introduction to GitHub Actions
foundations.why: Introduces what actions and workflows are, the workflow syntax elements and the events that start a workflow, the core theory this group builds on.

foundations.title: Introduction to GitHub administration
foundations.why: Explains GitHub authentication, organizations and permissions, the concepts behind choosing the scope and permissions a workflow gets.
foundations.evidence: How does GitHub organization and permissions work?

tasks.text: Configure workflows to run for scheduled, manual, webhook, and repository events

picks.title: Automate development tasks by using GitHub Actions
picks.why: The module teaches how to build a basic GitHub Actions workflow, which a learner needs before configuring when workflows run; it does not name the scheduled, manual or webhook triggers itself.

picks.title: Manage GitHub Actions in the enterprise

foundations.why: Overview of what GitHub Actions workflows do in a repository, the basic concept behind the jobs and steps this group teaches.
foundations.evidence: Create workflows within your repository to build, test, package, release, and deploy to Azure.
